title: One earthquake made Earth's day shorter 🌏
subject: earthquake
description:
Could another quake like this change the planet again? 👇

On December 26, 2004, a magnitude 9 earthquake off Sumatra triggered the Indian Ocean tsunami. NASA's Richard Gross and Benjamin Fong Chao calculated that the shifted rock shortened Earth's day by 2.68 microseconds, moved the mean North Pole about 2.5 centimeters toward 145 degrees East, and made the planet slightly less flattened.

Sources: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory, "NASA Details Earthquake Effects on the Earth" (January 10, 2005); Nature News, "Sumatran quake sped up Earth's rotation" (Michael Hopkin, December 30, 2004); ScienceDaily (NASA/JPL release, January 2005).

scenes.text: One earthquake made every day on Earth shorter.
On December 26, 2004, the seafloor off Sumatra tore open: a magnitude 9 quake, the largest since 1964.
Its tsunami crossed the Indian Ocean, from Indonesia to Thailand and Sri Lanka.
NASA's Richard Gross and Benjamin Chao calculated what that moving rock did to the planet.
The day got 2.68 microseconds shorter, and the North Pole shifted about 2.5 centimeters.
Even Earth's shape changed, slightly rounder. Too small to detect, but not to calculate.
